patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents with a complaint of severe vulvar itching that has been gradually worsening over the course of the past year. She has attempted to use over-the-counter lubricants for relief with no substantial improvement. She reports severe pain during vaginal intercourse that has recently led to cessation of sexual activity.

Secondary_Symptoms: Use of over-the-counter lubricants with no relief

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diet-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide, menopause occurred at 52 years of age.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Sexually active with her husband until recently due to discomfort.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies urinary symptoms, abnormal vaginal discharge, or rectal symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic vulvar itching and discomfort.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“My main concern is severe itching of my vulva that’s been getting worse over the past year, and it doesn’t really improve with over-the-counter lubricants. I also have painful intercourse, so I’ve stopped having sex because of the discomfort.”
What is your age, and have you gone through menopause?
“I’m 60 years old, and I went through menopause about eight years ago.”
Have you noticed any changes in the appearance
“I have noticed the vulvar skin looks more irritated and a bit red, and the area feels tender and sometimes looks slightly swollen. I haven’t had any unusual discharge or bleeding, though.”

“Yes, I don’t really have any abnormal discharge or bleeding, just the persistent severe itching and the redness and tenderness. I’ve been told about yeast, but it hasn’t seemed to behave like an infection that would fully clear. Can you examine the area and help figure out what’s causing it?”
Have you noticed any white patches, thinning of the skin

“I haven’t really noticed clear white patches, but the skin does seem a bit more sensitive and possibly thinner than it used to be, and it feels tender. There are times when the redness is more noticeable, but no obvious bleeding or discharge.”
Have you noticed any similar itching, rashes, or sores

“I don’t get sores, but I do have intermittent irritation that feels like a rash—no open wounds. I haven’t noticed similar itching anywhere else on my skin or a spreading rash beyond the vulvar area.”
Have you noticed any changes in your urinary habits,

“No, I haven’t noticed any urinary changes—no burning, frequency, or urgency. It’s mainly the severe vulvar itching with redness and tenderness, and it hurts during intercourse, which is why I stopped.”

“I haven’t used any prescription creams yet—only over-the-counter products, which haven’t helped much. I’m worried it’s something chronic because it’s been steadily worsening for a year, and it’s really affecting sex.”
